context_requirements: Expression of PXR (NR1I2) or CAR for CYP induction
Hepatic or intestinal lineage for strong CYP and lipid gene responses
Functional mitochondrial membrane potential for toxicity-related transcriptional changes
Proliferating cells for cell-cycle arrest signatures
falsifiers: No change in CYP3A4, CYP2B6, or other CYP genes at 24 h in any line
No change in cholesterol synthesis genes (HMGCR, HMGCS1, FDFT1) at 24 h
No decrease in proliferation or cell-cycle genes at 24 h
No oxidative stress or apoptosis signature at 24 h
Transcriptional response indistinguishable from vehicle at both time points

evidence.supports: Efavirenz activates PXR and induces CYP and lipid genes, leading to hypercholesterolemia and hepatic steatosis
Efavirenz causes mitochondrial membrane depolarization and apoptosis in hepatoma cells
Efavirenz reduces neural stem cell proliferation and increases oxidative stress and apoptosis markers
Etravirine binds CDK2 and shows cytotoxic and cell-cycle effects in Huh-7 cells
